# **Analytics Dashboard — Proposal**

October 20, 2026

# **Summary**

We can build a leadership dashboard today that covers 25 of the 27 proposed metrics from the Zillow and underwriting data we already store. Four of those stay approximate until we record a history of deal status changes, and the last two need a source for client data.

The dashboard answers four leadership questions:

* How many new Zillow listings come in, and how many do we underwrite?

* Where is every deal in the pipeline right now?

* How many presented deals turn into client contracts, and how many do we lose to the market?

* Which markets and price ranges produce the best deals?

**The most important finding:** 766 of 931 deals marked "present to clients" (82%) are no longer for sale on Zillow. Only 134 deals are "client under contract". The dashboard should show how many presented deals went off the market without one of our clients under contract.

All numbers come from the development database snapshot (listing data through Oct 8, 2026). Production numbers will differ.

# **How the data connects**

![][image1]  
*How the Zillow and underwriting data connect (counts from the dev database)*

One Zillow listing can have several underwritings. The listing's Zillow status sets each deal's "pending" flag, and moving a deal to "present to clients" records the approver and the approval date.

# **What the data shows today**

The data supports most metrics, but approval dates, analyst assignments and client data are thin or missing.

| Fact | Value (dev DB) | What it means for the dashboard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Zillow listings collected | 14,582 from 172 (presets) | A solid base for daily intake numbers |
| Listings with at least one underwriting | 4,696 (32%) | "Underwriting coverage" |
| Underwritings | 3,444 new system, 2,021 old Google Sheet, 7 blank | Default to the new system, with a toggle for old data |
| Presented deals showing as no longer for sale | 766 of 931 (82%) | The "pending" flag must be split by real Zillow status |
| Deals under client contract | 134 | The win count for conversion rates |
| Approval date recorded | 115 new-system deals, 490 old-sheet deals | "Time to present" works only on a small sample for now |
| Analyst recorded on new-system deals | 929 of 3,444 | Analyst leaderboards will be incomplete |
| Same property underwritten more than once | 133 properties | The real "duplicate deals" number |
| Copies made with the Duplicate button | 9 | Separate from the 133 above |

The system stores only each deal's current status, not when it changed. So any funnel built today is a snapshot: a deal moved back from "present to clients" to "maybe" no longer counts as presented.

# **Proposed metrics**

29 metrics in seven groups. 21 are ready now, 5 are built on the new status history (8, 14, 27, 28, 29), 1 still works with caveats (13), and 2 need data we don't have yet.

| \# | Metric | How it is calculated | Feasibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | New listings per day and per week, by market or Presets | Listing first-seen date | Ready now |
| 2  | Underwriting coverage | New listings with an underwriting ÷ all new listings, plus median days from listing to underwriting | Ready now |
| 3 | Automated vs. manual underwritings | Count by the automated flag | Ready now |
| 4 | Automation health | Batch jobs succeeded, failed and queued; last run per saved search | Ready now |

# **Gaps to close first**

One small engineering change unlocks the four "caveats" metrics; the client data question unlocks the last two.

1. **Record every status change.** *Done: the status history is live on production (design: `docs/features/process_log/process_log.md`).* Add a status history table that saves the old status, new status, who changed it and when.

   * Unlocks: true funnels, time spent in each status, backlog age, and analyst cycle time (metrics 9, 13, 14, 27).

   * Cost: one database migration and a few lines of code.

   * It only records changes from the day it ships, so starting early matters.

2. **Find the client data source.** No client records exist in this database. We need to know whether they live in the CRM, the login system or elsewhere (metrics 16 and 17).

3. **Fix the "submitted" date.** The system no longer fills it in for new deals. Either record it when the analyst completes a deal, which gives analyst cycle time, or leave it off the dashboard.

4. **Decide how to treat old Google Sheet deals.** They make up 2,021 of 5,472 underwritings and use an old "previously underwritten" status. Default the dashboard to new-system deals, with a toggle to include old ones.

# **Decisions needed**

* Approve adding the status history table now, so funnel and timing metrics become accurate going forward.

* Confirm where client data lives, and who can give us access.

* Pick the 6 headline numbers for the top row of the dashboard.

* Agree on the purchase price ranges and the 6 stage groups in metric 7\.

* Confirm the dashboard should read production data, and how often it refreshes.
